result.title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation
result.summary: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Plücker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. A differentiable expectation over joint types and axis directions couples attribute reconstruction to the motion it induces. An image-conditioned flow learns the resulting functional latents, while a multi-state-adapted Gaussian model supplies appearance. At inference, recovered part assignments and joints articulate a single set of rest-pose Gaussians without regenerating the object for each state. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and ACD show stronger part-box agreement, articulated-state geometry and visual similarity than the compared baselines, while joint prediction reduces axis, origin and range errors relative to ArtiLatent. Controlled ablations support the joint-line encoding and show that motion supervision reduces anchor-motion error. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be released in the future.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 MoRE，用坐标对齐的关节线编码（轴分类加两个 Plücker 矩分量）从单张图像生成铰接 3D 物体，并在表示学习中通过解码关节移动锚点、与标注关节运动比对来约束编码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用可微期望把离散属性（关节类型、轴向）重构与其诱导的运动结果绑定，可能为 LVR 中离散 latent 假设的监督与贡献分配提供线索；但属 3D 生成领域，是否可迁移到视觉推理状态仍需核查。
